name: Tram 28 (Eléctrico 28)
tagline: A regular Carris public tram line through Graça, Alfama and Chiado: worth riding, if you plan around the queues

description.short: Tram 28E is an ordinary Carris public transport line, run with small 1930s-era trams, from Martim Moniz through Graça, Alfama, the Sé, Chiado and Estrela to Campo de Ourique (Prazeres). The ride is about an hour end to end. The nearest stop to the ship is Sé, about 13 minutes' walk uphill.
description.full:
Tram 28E is not a tourist attraction with a ticket office. It is a regular Carris public line, used by residents, that happens to climb through the most photogenic streets in Lisbon. That shapes everything about riding it on a port day.

The line runs from Martim Moniz up through Graça, down past the Portas do Sol and Santa Luzia viewpoints to the Sé, then through the Baixa, Chiado and Estrela to Campo de Ourique (Prazeres). End to end it takes about an hour.

From the ship, the nearest stop is Sé, by the cathedral, about 13 minutes' walk uphill from the terminal. Westbound trams reach Sé after climbing through Graça and Alfama, so they often arrive full and may not have room for more passengers. To get a seat, walk about 23 minutes to the Martim Moniz terminus. There the queue is the problem: from mid-morning to late afternoon it can take longer than the ride itself. Before about 09:30 it is usually much shorter.

Fares (Carris, 2026): buying on board costs €3.30 for a single ride, valid only on that tram. You can pay the driver in cash or tap a contactless bank card or MB Way at the validator. It is cheaper to buy a Navegante occasional card (€0.50) at a metro station and load either a Carris/Metro single journey (€1.90, unlimited Carris rides for 60 minutes) or a 24-hour Carris/Metro ticket (€7.25). The Lisboa Card also covers Carris trams.

Pickpockets work this line, especially in the crush at boarding and on crowded standing trips. Keep phones and wallets in front pockets or a zipped bag.

With limited time, a practical plan is to ride from Martim Moniz to Sé or Chiado (about 25 to 40 minutes), then walk down to the river. Skip it entirely if you arrive at a stop to find a long queue: the view from the Portas do Sol viewpoint is a short walk from Sé. Carris sometimes shortens or diverts the route for roadworks or events, so check carris.pt for service alerts on the day.
description.history: Electric trams replaced horse-drawn cars in Lisbon from 1901, run by Carris, the same company that operates the network today, and routes like the 28 were laid through neighbourhoods whose streets are too narrow and steep for buses. The small yellow cars used today are 'Remodelados': two-axle trams from the 1930s that Carris rebuilt in the 1990s with new motors, brakes and electrics while keeping the wooden bodywork. They survive because the modern articulated trams used on the riverside line 15E cannot handle the 28's tight curves and steep gradients.
description.significance: The 28 links in one ride most of the old hillside districts a cruise passenger hears about: Graça, Alfama, the Sé, Baixa, Chiado and Estrela. Because it is a working line, it is also the cheapest way to see them without walking uphill. Its popularity has a cost: residents often cannot board, which is one reason to ride it early and move on.

address.street: Praça Martim Moniz (eastern terminus) to Campo de Ourique/Prazeres (western terminus)

directions.general: Tram 28 route runs east-west across central Lisbon. Best boarding points: Martim Moniz (eastern terminus) or Campo de Ourique (western terminus) for better chance of getting a seat.
directions.fromCruisePort: The closest stop to the ship is Sé (the cathedral), about 13 minutes uphill from the terminal. To get a seat, walk about 23 minutes to the Martim Moniz terminus and board there.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 28 IS public transport. Access boarding points via Metro Green Line to Martim Moniz, or Blue Line to Terreiro do Paço then walk to downtown stops.
directions.parking: Not applicable - this is a tram experience, not a driving destination.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Runs daily as part of the Carris network

seasonal.hours: First departure from Martim Moniz around 05:40; service until around midnight
seasonal.notes: Timetable in force from 1 June 2026. Daytime trams roughly every 10 minutes. About 1 hour end to end.

seasonal.hours: First departure from Martim Moniz around 05:45; service ends earlier in the evening than on weekdays
seasonal.notes: Check the Carris timetable and service alerts for diversions or bus replacement on the day.

admissionPrices.notes: Carris 2026 fares: on-board single ride €3.30 (cash to the driver, contactless bank card or MB Way at the validator; valid only on that tram). With a Navegante occasional card (€0.50): Carris/Metro journey €1.90 (unlimited Carris rides for 60 minutes), 24-hour Carris/Metro ticket €7.25, or Zapping pay-as-you-go €1.72 per ride. Free with the Lisboa Card.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 25–40 minutes for a useful section (Martim Moniz to Sé or Chiado); about 1 hour end to end
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Before 09:30, when the Martim Moniz queue is short. Late evening is also quieter, but may not suit a port day.
busyPeriods: Mid-morning to late afternoon every day
Days with several cruise ships in port
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Treat the 28 as a public tram, not a hop-on hop-off tour: every time you get off, you pay again unless you hold a time-based ticket. Board early at Martim Moniz, keep valuables secure, and be ready to give up your seat to older residents. If the queue is long, walk the route instead: Sé to Portas do Sol takes about 10 minutes uphill.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: 2–3 hours: about 23 minutes' walk to Martim Moniz, queue time, a 25–40 minute ride to Sé or Chiado, then about 15–25 minutes' walk back down to the terminal
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Moderate to difficult. The nearest stop (Sé) is 13 minutes uphill from the terminal. Trams have high steps and are not wheelchair accessible; standing trips are crowded and jolting.
combinableWith: Miradouro das Portas do Sol and Miradouro de Santa Luzia
tips: Be at Martim Moniz before 09:30 to board with little or no queue; from mid-morning the wait can be longer than the ride.
Load a Navegante occasional card (€0.50) at a metro machine with a Carris/Metro journey (€1.90, 60 minutes) or a 24-hour ticket (€7.25) instead of paying €3.30 on board.
The on-board €3.30 ticket is valid only on that tram; if you get off, you pay again on the next one.
Boarding at Sé is closest to the ship, but westbound trams often arrive full after climbing through Alfama.
Keep phones and wallets in front pockets or a zipped bag: pickpockets target the crowds at boarding and in the aisle.
Ride Martim Moniz to Chiado (about 40 minutes), then walk down Rua do Carmo and the Baixa to the river: the walk back to the terminal is flat from Praça do Comércio.
If the 28 queue is long, tram 12E runs a short loop from Martim Moniz via the Sé and Limoeiro with the same type of vintage tram.
Check carris.pt for service alerts on the day: sections of the 28E are periodically replaced by buses during roadworks.

highlights: Regular Carris public line, not a tour: €3.30 on board, or €1.90 with a Navegante card
About 1 hour end to end, Martim Moniz to Campo de Ourique (Prazeres)
Passes the Portas do Sol and Santa Luzia viewpoints, the Sé, Chiado and Estrela
Climbs and squeezes through streets too narrow for buses
Nearest stop to the ship: Sé, about 13 minutes uphill from the terminal
Included in the Lisboa Card and in 24-hour Carris/Metro tickets
facilities: Small number of seats; most passengers stand
Hand straps and rails for standing passengers
On-board validator for Navegante cards, contactless bank cards and MB Way

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Not wheelchair accessible. Boarding is by high steps, and standing passengers are thrown about on sharp curves and steep descents. Very crowded conditions make it difficult for anyone with limited mobility or balance.

languages: No commentary: this is public transport, not a tour
